answers.answer: Shuffle all four III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle the nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle the three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return the unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘face-down 10-card Conflict Deck’; return unused Conflict cards ‘without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In four players, start at 1 VP; in three players, start at 0 VP. Both setups give a human two Agents on the Leader and a third (Swordmaster) beside the board, 12 troops total (three in the garrison and nine in supply), and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: Score track ‘on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0’; two Agents on Leader; 12 troop cubes; ‘Take 1 water.’

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but taking a Reveal turn ends your turns for the phase; you cannot take an Agent turn afterward that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from the remaining hand, not Agent-played cards. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘Agent turns are optional’; ‘Once you’ve taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped’; Reveal effects are of ‘just-revealed cards only.’

answers.answer: Before placement, you may play a legal Plot Intrigue and use resources it grants to pay the entry cost. Resources from the Agent card or destination effects occur after placement and cannot pay that same cost. One card sends only one Agent, using one chosen matching icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot effects before placement can join available resources; gains ‘only after placement’ cannot pay entry; ‘one card can’t send multiple Agents.’

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy the three troops recruited that turn plus at most two from the four already in your garrison, for five total. At a non-Combat space you cannot normally deploy. Recruited troops come from your supply and are put in your garrison until deployed.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: deploy ‘any or all units recruited during your current turn’ plus ‘up to two more’ from garrison; recruit from supply into garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a space connected to a post where you have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent, but not your own. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy after placing your Agent to draw a card, and must be chosen immediately after placement before space or Agent-card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both; two different Spies can be used for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spy Agent icon ‘do not recall’; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather Intelligence is decided ‘immediately after placing your Agent’; cannot recall same Spy for both.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm 3, and four swords 4. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0, regardless of swords. With no unit in the Conflict, you are ineligible for Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop = 2, sandworm = 3, sword = 1; ‘must have at least one unit’; Combat Intrigue: player needs ‘at least one unit.’

answers.answer: Yes. Passing once does not prevent acting again; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: ‘not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; close after consecutive passes; cleanup returns troops to supply and resets markers.

answers.answer: In both cases each of the two tied for first gets the second reward, and nobody takes the Conflict card. In a four-player game the remaining players compete for the third reward; in a three-player game there are no other rewards. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first in four players leaves others to compete for third; with three or fewer, no other rewards; nobody takes card; ‘0 strength receives no reward.’

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; multiple worms do not multiply the doubling further, so two worms do not quadruple rewards. Control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. If a reward is pay 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay 3 again for a second VP (or 6 spice for 2 VP).
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘one or more sandworms, double’; control and battle icons cannot; may pay cost a second time.

answers.answer: After winning a Conflict and taking its card face up into your supply, check for a matching battle icon on another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. Matching is mandatory: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, the wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take card, check another face-up Conflict or Objective; ‘must flip’; Endgame wild may match any icon.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first to 4 also takes the Alliance and its 1 VP; an opponent tying the holder does not take it—must rise above. If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied player takes it (holder chooses recipient if several were tied); if holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, it returns to the board. Alliance VP follows possession.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: 2 VP reverses below 2; 4 track bonus retained; first to 4 takes Alliance; ‘tying ... does not steal’; FAQ transfer on holder losing Influence.

answers.answer: Spend Persuasion during the Reveal turn before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card and split one source across cards. The Row refills to five, so after buying a card you may buy its replacement if affordable. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile; unused Persuasion is lost.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Persuasion at any point in Reveal; pool/split; Row always five; acquired card goes face up to discard; cannot save Persuasion.

answers.answer: At Makers, each unoccupied Maker space gains one spice on its bonus spot; when visited, you gain all accumulated bonus spice. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are required only where specified and are retained, not spent. The Shield Wall prevents summoning at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while present; once removed, worms may be summoned to any Conflict. A worm can never go into a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers: unoccupied spaces add spice; ‘gain all’ bonus; Sandworms and Shield Wall sections give restrictions and choices.

answers.answer: At Recall, if any player has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty, Endgame is triggered. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then highest VP wins. Resource tiebreakers in order are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring: ‘At the end of a round’; first resolve Endgame Intrigue; tiebreak order spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

answers.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contracts face down, reveal two, and put the other 18 face down in the bank. Add four Intrigue and four Imperium cards to their decks. Shaddam is an optional Leader, not required. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix and stay in the box for standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup: 20 contracts, ‘flip two face up’; shuffle 4 additional cards into each deck; Shaddam option; contrasting-back set left in box.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the icon lets you take one of two face-up contracts and replace it from the bank face up; without CHOAM, or when none remain, it gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the shown spice total that turn, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Taking contracts and Completing contracts specify each completion condition.

answers.answer: No. You must have held the board-space contract when sending the Agent, so a contract acquired after visiting waits until a future turn. On completion announce it, gain its rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Completing contracts: if already sent Agent, ‘wait until a future turn’; announce, gain rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. It receives the Ornithopter Objective; the humans receive the other two eligible Objectives, and the human whose card shows First Player takes the marker. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human; First Player alternates only between humans. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Setup: ‘one shared scoring Rival’; Rival gets Ornithopter; order listed; ‘The Rival never Reveals.’

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of its specified type, otherwise ignore it, then immediately reveal another card either way. Ignore normal destination costs and effects; apply only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination and reveal again; Place Spy cards trigger another reveal; ignore normal space costs/effects; reshuffle on empty/Reshuffle.

answers.answer: Shuffle the Objective cards after removing those marked for a different player count; give each player one eligible Objective face up. The player whose Objective shows First Player takes the marker. Shaddam may not be used without CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched count, shuffle eligible cards, distribute face up; Shaddam ‘Do not use ... unless playing with CHOAM.’

answers.answer: Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; make a convenient substitution if the bank runs out. Troops are limited by each player’s supply: if it is empty, that player cannot recruit more until troops return there. Resource gains come from the bank and payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup: resources and worms ‘not meant to be limited’; troop supply restriction; gains from bank and payments returned to it.

answers.answer: The phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Round Start reveals a Conflict first, then each player draws five cards. At Recall, check for Endgame; if none, return Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and begin the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists five phases; Round Start reveals Conflict then draws five; Recall prepares next round.

answers.answer: Yes. Board-space, Agent-box, and Faction Influence effects may be resolved in any order. But all space costs and requirements must be paid/met immediately before resolving any space or played-card effects, so the visit’s Influence cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: costs before resolving effects; effects may occur in any order; Faction advance listed after effects.

answers.answer: Normally an arrow cost/effect can be used only once per turn, so an optional arrow cost cannot be paid twice for repeated effects. Most card and space effects are mandatory; exceptions include ‘may,’ optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play it; optional arrows can be declined, but then do not grant the effect. Doubled Conflict rewards are the exception to the once-per-turn arrow limit.
answers.evidence: Arrows: cost/effect once per turn, except doubled Conflict rewards; FAQ Mandatory effects and costs describes optional/mandatory cases.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have none in supply, you may first recall one of your own Spies for no effect. If the placement effect requires a particular Agent-icon type connected to that post, you must meet it or cannot place the Spy.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy icon places on unoccupied post; if none in supply may recall one; specified Agent icon must connect.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate bypasses only another player’s Agent, not your own. A Spy does not let you take an Agent turn by itself: ordinary Agent turn still requires playing a card. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you may use different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Infiltrate cannot bypass own Agent; Gather Intelligence requires placement; same Spy cannot pay both; FAQ recalling Spy requires playing a card.

answers.answer: Whenever anyone visits a controlled location, its controller gets the bonus (1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery; 1 spice at Imperial Basin), separately from the visitor’s effects; a controller visiting also gets both. A Conflict winner at that location places a Control marker, replacing the previous one. When the Conflict is revealed for a location already controlled, its controller may deploy one troop from supply without visiting.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations: controller receives bonus whenever any player visits; winning control replaces marker; reveal defensive troop from supply.

answers.answer: For a tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; first-place winner keeps first reward and Conflict card, and no further rewards are given. Players tied for third get nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets second reward, nobody takes the card, and no other rewards are given (including to a fourth player).
answers.evidence: Combat ties table: second tie and third tie rows; three tied first clarified as no other rewards in either 3- or 4-player game.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three distinct positive strengths, first and second place get their rewards; third gets none. This is also true with a two-player game’s Rival as third competitor: 2–3-player reward rules apply, with the Rival counted as a player.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with 2 or 3 players, ordinary first and second receive rewards; third only in a tie for second; includes Rival game.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat Intrigues only during Combat; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down and separate from your deck; after resolving, put them face up in the Intrigue discard pile. If the deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards section and FAQ Draw timing: types/timing, face-down separate, face-up discard; exhausted deck is reshuffled.

answers.answer: No, an ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot discard Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Secrets’ steal effect takes one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has at least four.
answers.evidence: Discarding: from hand, not Intrigue unless specified; Intrigue cards: Steal icon random from each opponent with 4+.

answers.answer: Trashing may remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary cards to the box and Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or explicitly directed (including self-trash). Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove its acquired VP; that VP is retained.
answers.evidence: Trashing section; FAQ Victory: Spice Must Flow acquire VP is retained if card later trashed.

answers.answer: Acquire-box effects resolve once, when acquiring the card. If your deck is empty when a draw is needed, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Unused Persuasion is lost and cannot be carried forward.
answers.evidence: Acquire box resolves ‘at the moment you acquire’; Acquiring Cards says Persuasion never saved; reshuffle discard when deck empty.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed during your Reveal turn remain in play until Clean Up unless trashed first. Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play, so two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of order. They cease being in play when moved to discard at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: other Fremen cards in play; Bond cards can activate each other; cards remain until Clean Up.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just sent; you may use the recalled Agent on a later Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop goes from Conflict to your garrison. ‘Retreat any number’ can mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon returns ‘other’ Agent and may be reused same round; Retreat; FAQ says retreat any number allows zero.

answers.answer: A free-choice gain of two Influence applies both to one chosen Faction; it cannot be split between two. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token; a minimum-Influence effect requires reaching the stated level with that Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence: free choice of two cannot choose different Factions; Alliance icon requires token; cards may require minimum Influence.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if multiple opponents were tied, the former holder chooses the recipient. If the holder drops to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board and the old holder loses its 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Official FAQ Alliance loss: formerly tied player takes token; if several, holder chooses; on fall below 4 with none at 4+, return token.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is revealed and used immediately that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the next five-card draw. A Plot Intrigue whose effect applies at Reveal stays face up until then, is used, and then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing: during Reveal ‘immediately reveal and use’; after Reveal keep for next round; Plot stays face up until Reveal then discarded.

answers.answer: No. After tying for first you did not win, so you cannot play a ‘when you win a Conflict’ Intrigue. If you receive it as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: cannot play after tying; if received as winning reward, may play immediately.

answers.answer: If VP and all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed 12-space track.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory: if all four tiebreakers tied, most recent Reveal wins; ‘Scores may exceed ... 12.’

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts you hold for that same space with the one Agent placement. Contract effects are another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with board-space and Agent-box effects, but you must already hold them when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion is mandatory: fulfill all same-space contracts with one placement; resolve in any order; must hold at placement.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contract(s); when acquiring a contract, Sardaukar Commander lets him choose a set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of a generally available one. His Emperor of the Known Universe restriction starts immediately when Signet Ring is played to send an Agent and applies for that turn only, not the round.
answers.evidence: FAQ Shaddam: contracts ‘do not start in your possession’; restriction takes effect immediately and lasts for that turn.

answers.answer: Feyd’s token starts on the leftmost space of his Training track and remains on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica starts Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Feyd token start/end; Lady Jessica begins face up; Reverend Mother Jessica may act on flip turn.

answers.answer: Yes, moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2, and you can reach 2 with that Faction again later by losing Influence and regaining it. Moving downward through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications for Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild’s Favor specify these cases.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade access; it always draws one card and gives a contract with CHOAM, otherwise 2 Solari (also 2 Solari if contracts are exhausted). Dutiful Service uses Emperor access; it gives one Emperor Influence and a contract with CHOAM, otherwise 2 Solari. Accept Contract has no automatic Faction advance; Dutiful Service automatically advances Emperor Influence by one, counted once total.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide and Faction status: Accept Contract non-Faction, Dutiful Service Emperor; table lists their effects.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City, no entry cost, Combat space; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, plus controller gets 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen, no cost, Combat space; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw one card. Research Station: City, costs 2 water, Combat space; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and gives all bonus spice plus a choice of 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water and gives all bonus spice plus a choice of 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Hooks are not spent when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table; Maker Hooks retained, not spent, when summoning.

answers.answer: Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option grants no troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Sietch Tabr row lists both choices and no cost; second has no recruit.

answers.answer: High Council is Landsraad and not a Combat space. Each visit costs 5 Solari. First visit puts your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Later visits grant 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster uses Landsraad access and is not Combat. It costs 8 Solari before anyone obtains Swordmaster, then 6 Solari once anyone has one. Each player may gain it only once; the new Agent is available this round and thereafter. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster row.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, costs 3 Solari, and requires 2+ Emperor Influence; it is not Combat. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, then recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically advance Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Privilege row; table lists no Faction advance.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, costs 3 spice, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and is not Combat. It grants 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad and not Combat: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops either way, and if you pay 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City and Combat: choose 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari for free or 4 Solari if paying 1 spice. Its controller separately gains 1 Solari on the visit.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Gather Support and Spice Refinery rows.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild Combat space, costs 5 spice, gives 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops. Desert Tactics: Fremen Combat space, costs 1 water, gives 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop, and optionally trashes a card. Sardaukar: Emperor, not Combat, costs 4 spice, gives 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue, and recruits four troops. Only the first two permit normal deployment.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar; Combat column marked Yes/No.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall: Landsraad, no cost, not Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during Reveal if your Agent is there. Espionage: Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies: Spacing Guild, no cost, not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it may be played even if no opposing Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when the card gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ Leader card rulings: False Orders and Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it is not acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate ruling states all three consequences.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four Influence cubes at track bottoms, three troops in garrison and the rest in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, and 1 water; score and Combat markers are 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. It is a scoring Rival: its 10+ VP triggers Endgame and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival setup and scoring rules; ‘retaining the 2P Reshuffle card’; it can win at 10+ VP.

answers.answer: As soon as the Rival’s total of Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water reaches its printed Swordmaster threshold, it spends that many resources and takes its third Agent, usable that round. Resources count one each; spend Solari first, then spice, Intrigue, water; leftovers remain. The new Agent is immediately available in the current round.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster section.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, the Rival spends each qualifying set for 1 VP: 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water. These are separate resource-set thresholds; a mixed total of seven does not qualify.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources: whenever it has ‘7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water,’ spend each such set for 1 VP.

answers.answer: When it chooses Influence, Rival uses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains normal VP for reaching 2 and gains/loses Alliance VP as a human does, but receives no resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in the Rival card’s Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Combat: gains/losses Influence VP and Alliances like human; no 4-Influence resource bonus; least Influence/tie order; numbered icon definition.

answers.answer: No. A two-destination card uses only the destination selected by current conditions; if that one is occupied, reveal a new card without using the other destination. Conditions are Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping and Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: select only the destination matching current conditions; if occupied reveal new card; conditions enumerated.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Recruited troops at a noncombat space go to its garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus not met is simply ignored and does not prevent placement.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: Combat deploy up to two garrison troops even when card recruited none; conditional bonus lack ‘never prevents placing.’

answers.answer: For an unrestricted Spy post, use the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes section.

answers.answer: If its Scheme recruits troops before the Agent placement and it then visits a Combat space that turn, deploy those recruited troops too. A Place Spy card with no legal post is ignored, and the Rival reveals another Hagal card because it did not send an Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes: Scheme recruits deploy if same-turn Combat; Place Spy always prompts next reveal.

answers.answer: The Rival takes all accumulated bonus spice at any visited Maker space. At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, if it has Hooks and the Conflict permits worms, it summons one or two worms respectively instead of taking base spice. Without Hooks or when worms are blocked by the Shield Wall, it takes base spice (Hagga 2, Deep Desert 4); Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces specifies bonus spice, worm choice and base spice if none summoned.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal a Hagal card and add its bottom swords as strength; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. This happens before humans’ normal Combat Intrigue window, so humans may respond afterward. With no deployed unit, it does not receive the bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: at beginning, if at least one unit, reveal one Hagal card; Reshuffle repeat; then humans have normal window.

answers.answer: Yes. The Rival can gain control bonuses, a defensive troop when its controlled Conflict is revealed, normal battle-icon VP, and doubled rewards with worms. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. With CHOAM, it never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat section states control, defensive troop, rewards, optional VP, and contract behavior.

answers.answer: During Reveal effects, total and announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point while resolving; update it as needed later in that turn. If over 20, flip to the +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn and Strength: set at any point while resolving, updating as needed; strength over 20 flips marker to +20 side.

answers.answer: A Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not when you merely reveal it. Card text can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader abilities: Signet Ring ability activates when playing Signet Ring on Agent turn; overview says any type cards can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon on a card returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for an effect. It does not by itself mean Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate Spy uses without a card icon.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts defines Recall Spy icon; separate Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence effects.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard-a-card instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand, but cannot select an Intrigue unless specified; it does not trash it.
answers.evidence: Trashing: separate trash-an-Intrigue icon; Discarding: Intrigue excluded unless specified.

answers.answer: A doubled reward of ‘gain 1 Influence of your choice’ gives two Influence, and you may choose the same Faction or two different Factions. A single effect granting two Influence with free choice must put both in one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm doubling example allows 2 Influence with same Faction or two different; Influence rule says a single free-choice gain two cannot split.

answers.answer: Resolve the Signet Ring ability printed on the Rival’s selected Rival card, as part of its Hagal effect. The Rival does not need a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn; it never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Rival rules: follow printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; Rival never takes a Reveal turn.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon gives the Rival one token only if it lacks one; if it already has one, it takes no additional token. Shield Wall removal works only if Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks it is ignored, and if Wall already gone it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table lists each state/result.

answers.answer: Secrets is Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost, and is not Combat. It gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck. Also, each opponent with at least four Intrigues gives one selected at random to you.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets row.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no cost, and is a Combat space. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there. The controller separately gains 1 spice; if visitor and controller are the same player, that player receives both amounts.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Basin row; preamble says visitor and controller effects both resolve even if same player.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards remaining from earlier rounds; those older cards stay there. Each player draws five cards after the Conflict is revealed.
answers.evidence: Round Start: reveal Conflict and place it next to deck ‘on top of any Conflict cards remaining’; ‘Then each player draws five.’

answers.answer: Each human places one cube on the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. Alliance tokens begin on their marked spaces on the four tracks, so no player starts holding one. The Shield Wall token starts in its marked area below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6: Alliance tokens on tracks; cubes at bottom spaces; Shield Wall on board.

answers.answer: The First Player takes the first turn, then players proceed clockwise, one turn at a time. A player who Reveals is skipped for the rest of the phase; in 3–4 player play Player Turns ends when all players have Revealed. During Combat Intrigue, First Player has priority and order continues clockwise. An eligible player may play any number, or pass; after passing they may act again if another player plays, and the window ends after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat Intrigue describe clockwise order, phase end, priority, any number, and consecutive passes.

answers.answer: The steps are: Reveal Cards (reveal remaining hand); Resolve Reveal Effects (resolve just-revealed cards, acquire with Persuasion, set strength); Clean Up (move all cards in front of you to discard). Effects may be resolved in any order, not necessarily card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn lists three steps; Resolve Reveal Effects says effects ‘in any order.’

answers.answer: Shuffle each human’s ten-card starting deck and place it face down in their supply. Remove CHOAM-marked cards from Intrigue and Imperium decks; shuffle each separately face down. Deal five Imperium cards face up into the Row and keep the rest face down. Put Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Combat markers start at 0; three Spies and Councilor start in supply; Control markers start in supply.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4 and 6; Initial card states; components placement; Combat marker 0 and other components in supply.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, Persuasion ordinarily buys cards from the five-card Imperium Row or either Reserve stack, Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow. Each card’s cost is at its top right. These ordinary Persuasion purchases happen during Reveal.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards section states eligible Row/Reserve cards, top-right cost, and Reveal timing.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional, even if a legal placement or recall exists. A Shield Wall destruction icon may be declined; if removed, the Wall returns to the box and cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: ordinary placement and Recall Spy optional; Shield Wall: may remove, gone for rest of game.

answers.answer: The card played must have a matching Agent icon for the destination, and you choose one icon. A Spy connected to Shipping does not give a City-only card access to Shipping. If the card has the Spy Agent icon, it can send the Agent to any space connected to a post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn matching requirement; Spy Agent icon provides connected-post access; a connected Spy alone does not give every card access.

answers.answer: Yes. On an Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before placement join your available resources and can pay entry. Resources gained after placement from the played Agent card or destination cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: may first play Plot Intrigue before placing Agent; pre-placement gains can pay; post-placement gains cannot.

answers.answer: No. Once both humans have Revealed, skip their turns but continue the Rival’s Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply. Combat begins only after both humans have Revealed and Rival has used all Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns two-player rule says precisely this; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: When a Conflict card is revealed for a location already controlled, its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict; it is optional and requires no Agent visit. After Conflict rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Round Start defensive bonus; Critical Locations: may deploy from supply; Combat cleanup says markers reset to 0.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching space. Resolve that card’s Agent box, not Reveal box, plus space effects. You cannot reuse a card already in play or in discard, nor move an Agent already on board; an Agent turn uses an Agent at your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play a card from hand; send Agent from Leader; resolve Agent box; Recall returns other Agents to Leader.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent, so he cannot postpone it by ordering board-space effects first.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Shaddam restriction ‘takes effect immediately’; general effect-order freedom cannot postpone it.

answers.answer: With four distinct positive strengths and four players, first, second, and third place each receive their printed rewards; fourth gets none. The highest-strength player wins the Conflict and takes its card face up, then checks for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: four-player first, second and third receive rewards; winner takes Conflict card; third/fourth delineation.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup: each player takes a Leader ‘(choose, or select at random).’

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your discard pile into a new deck if needed. You cannot choose a card directly from the discard pile. The separate Intrigue draw icon draws from the Intrigue Deck.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards: ordinary draw from own deck, reshuffle discard if empty; separate Intrigue draw uses Intrigue Deck.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card in the deck. It is not removed.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Setup: ‘Shuffle House Hagal ... retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.’

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A player who acquires one moves it from the bank to their garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup: put all 4 tokens in common bank; later acquired token moves onto player’s garrison.

answers.answer: Yes. If a Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise alters strength, adjust the Combat marker when that card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. The adjusted strength on the track is used to resolve rewards; the Reveal value is not fixed through the round.
answers.evidence: Combat phase: Combat marker adjusts ‘when that card resolves’; Reveal total ‘is not fixed for the rest of the round.’

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice, and water come from the bank. You do not take them from another player’s supply.
answers.evidence: Setup: whenever you gain these resources, take them from the bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contracts face down, then flip two face up for the board offers; put the other 18 face down in the bank. Players do not choose the offers or preset the bank order.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup: ‘Shuffle the 20 contracts face down, then flip two face up’; remaining 18 face down in bank.
